record.context_brief: Sharpness of lower bounds for chi_hat(Z_n,3)
record.original_question: For cyclic groups Z_n, determine whether the known lower bounds for the three-term restricted critical number chi_hat(Z_n, 3) are always sharp. More precisely, if n has a prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3 and p is the smallest such divisor, does chi_hat(Z_n, 3) always equal (1 + 1/p)n/3 + 3 when n = p, (1 + 1/p)n/3 + 2 when n = 3p, and (1 + 1/p)n/3 + 1 otherwise? If n has no prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3, does chi_hat(Z_n, 3) always equal floor(n/3) + 4 when 9 divides n and floor(n/3) + 3 otherwise?

evidence.quote: if n >= 16 and has prime divisors congruent to 2 mod 3 and p is the smallest such divisor, then chi_hat(Z_n, 3) >= (1 + 1/p) * n/3 + 3 if n = p, >= (1 + 1/p) * n/3 + 2 if n = 3p, and >= (1 + 1/p) * n/3 + 1 otherwise; and if n has no prime divisors congruent to 2 mod 3, then chi_hat(Z_n, 3) >= floor(n/3) + 4 if n is divisible by 9, and >= floor(n/3) + 3 otherwise.
We also believe that, actually, equality holds above for all n - this is certainly the case if n is even or prime; we have verified this (by computer) for all n <= 50.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{Z}_n$ denote the cyclic group of integers modulo $n$. For a subset $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_n$, let
$$3^{\wedge}A=\{a_1+a_2+a_3 : a_1,a_2,a_3\in A,\ a_1,a_2,a_3 \text{ pairwise distinct}\}.$$
Define the three-term restricted critical number
$$\widehat{\chi}(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)=\min\{|A| : A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_n,\ 3^{\wedge}A=\mathbb{Z}_n\}.$$
Prove or disprove the following equalities for all integers $n\ge 16$:

(I) Suppose $n$ has at least one prime divisor congruent to $2\pmod 3$, and let $p$ be the smallest such divisor. Then
$$\widehat{\chi}(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)=\begin{cases}\bigl(1+\tfrac{1}{p}\bigr)\tfrac{n}{3}+3 & \text{if } n=p,\\[2pt] \bigl(1+\tfrac{1}{p}\bigr)\tfrac{n}{3}+2 & \text{if } n=3p,\\[2pt] \bigl(1+\tfrac{1}{p}\bigr)\tfrac{n}{3}+1 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

(II) Suppose $n$ has no prime divisor congruent to $2\pmod 3$. Then
$$\widehat{\chi}(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)=\begin{cases}\lfloor n/3\rfloor+4 & \text{if } 9\mid n,\\[2pt] \lfloor n/3\rfloor+3 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

In each case the lower bound $\ge$ is known; the question is whether equality always holds.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published proof or refutation of the conjectured sharpness of these lower bounds for the three-term restricted critical number $\widehat{\chi}(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)$. Equality is known for $n$ even or prime and was verified computationally for $n\le 50$, but the general case appears not to be settled in the sources found.

status_evidence.title: Three-fold Restricted Set Addition in Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Work on three-fold restricted set addition in abelian groups, related to bounds on three-term restricted sumsets.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on three-fold restricted sumsets exists, but no explicit confirmation of sharpness of the stated bounds for all n was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Surveys restricted sumset results including Erdős–Heilbronn and Dias da Silva–Hamidoune bounds.
status_evidence.claim: General references on restricted sumsets do not record a resolution of the conjectured equality for chi_hat(Z_n,3).
